# iliad-029 — new renderings (5.217–317)

Rows are in the format of the table in `conventions.md`: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose. No line of this part stands in a published Odyssey unit, so there is no departure from the Odyssey English. Lines 5.229, 5.251, 5.259 and 5.283 are whole published units and take their published English unchanged; 5.280 and 5.312 stand inside longer published units and are reused for the lines concerned (5.312 with the Greek of the line: “if not then sharply had noticed the daughter of Zeus, Aphrodite”).

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Αἰνείας Τρώων ἀγὸς ἀντίον ηὔδα (5.217, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him then in turn Aeneas, leader of the Trojans, spoke, face to face:" | "Then Aeneas, leader of the Trojans, spoke to him in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for ἀμείβετο); follows the table's 4.265 row (Idomeneus, Κρητῶν ἀγός) |
| Τρώων ἀγός (5.217) | "leader of the Trojans" | "leader of the Trojans" | "captain", "chief"; ἀγός "leader" as in the table's Κρητῶν ἀγός |
| αὐτίκα/αἶψα … ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (5.242, αἶψα δὲ Τυδεΐδην …) | "and at once to Tydeus’-son winged words he spoke:" | "and at once he spoke winged words to the son of Tydeus:" | the table's ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα unchanged (4.69 "At once he spoke winged words to Athena") |
| κραιπνὰ μάλ’ (adverbial neuter plural, 5.223) | "very much in a rush" | "how well they know how to rush" (μάλα carried by "well") | "swiftly" (reserved for ὠκύς, θοός), "rapidly"; keeps the Odyssey's κραιπνός "rushing" |
| καμπύλον ἅρμα (5.231) | "the bent chariot" | "the bent chariot" | "curved chariot" (the iliad-028 `l` for ἀγκύλα τόξα), "curving"; καμπύλος "bent" as in the table's καμπύλα τόξα; the note says Homer does not say which part is curved |
| ὄχεσφιν (ἵπποισιν καὶ ὄχεσφιν, 5.219; ἐμῶν ὀχέων, 5.221) | "with horses and with chariot" · "my chariot" | "with horses and chariot" · "my chariot" | "chariots" (the table’s 4.297 row ἵπποισιν καὶ ὄχεσφι "with horses and chariots" is for many horsemen; here the speakers have one car, and the note says the plural stands for one vehicle) |

| μώνυχας ἵππους (5.236; μώνυξ "with an undivided hoof") | "solid-hoofed horses" | "the solid-hoofed horses" | "single-hoofed" (reads as one hoof per animal), "whole-hoofed", "strong-hoofed"; the Odyssey table’s μώνυχες ἵπποι, unchanged |
